events.title: ECMAScript 2020 standardized
events.summary: Ecma adopted ECMAScript 2020 in June 2020 — adding optional chaining, nullish coalescing, `BigInt`, and `Promise.allSettled`.
events.about: ES2020 features became everyday JavaScript: `obj?.prop` and `value ?? fallback` reduced null-pointer bugs; `BigInt` handled large integers; dynamic `import()` improved code splitting. Every modern bundler and browser targets these additions.

narrative.whyChosen: ES2020 delivered some of the most-used syntax sugar in modern JavaScript.
narrative.whyImportant: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing changed how millions of developers handle missing data.
narrative.problemSolved: Accessing nested properties and defaulting null/undefined values required verbose, error-prone boilerplate.

events.title: OpenAI GPT-3 API announced
events.summary: OpenAI announced API access to GPT-3 on June 11, 2020 — opening large-language-model text generation to developers beyond research previews.
events.about: The GPT-3 API let apps call a 175B-parameter model for completion, summarization, and code generation via HTTP. It launched the LLM API economy — copywriting tools, coding assistants, and chatbots built on a single endpoint before ChatGPT's consumer interface.

narrative.whyChosen: The GPT-3 API was the commercial inflection point for LLMs in production software.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved developers would pay per token for generative AI at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams could not ship LLM features without training and hosting their own massive models.

events.title: Sanfilippo steps down from Redis
events.summary: Salvatore Sanfilippo (antirez) stepped down as Redis maintainer on June 30, 2020, handing the project to a community team.
events.about: Sanfilippo built Redis alone from 2009 into infrastructure powering caches, queues, and real-time systems worldwide. His departure sparked discussion about maintainer burnout and corporate sponsorship of open source.

narrative.whyChosen: antirez stepping down was a landmark maintainer transition in open source.
narrative.whyImportant: It highlighted sustainability issues for solo-authored critical infrastructure.
narrative.problemSolved: Redis needed governance beyond one developer as adoption reached hyperscale.

events.title: Drupal 9 released
events.summary: Drupal 9.0 shipped on June 3, 2020 — a major version that removed deprecated code and updated Symfony and Twig dependencies while keeping the Drupal 8 architecture.
events.about: Drupal 9 was designed as a smooth upgrade from Drupal 8 — same APIs, updated vendor libraries, and no feature rewrites. It gave enterprise sites a supported path before Symfony 4 end-of-life forced migration to Drupal 10.

narrative.whyChosen: Drupal 9 extended the Symfony-based architecture with a low-friction upgrade from Drupal 8.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept enterprise Drupal sites on supported dependencies through 2023.
narrative.problemSolved: Drupal 8 sites faced end-of-life without a clear migration path that preserved custom modules.

events.title: Compound launches COMP governance token
events.summary: Compound distributed its COMP governance token starting June 15, 2020 — rewarding users who lent and borrowed on the protocol and kicking off "DeFi Summer."
events.about: Yield farming — earning governance tokens for providing liquidity — spread across Aave, Curve, and copycat protocols within weeks. TVL exploded as developers composed money legos: deposit DAI, borrow ETH, stake LP tokens, claim rewards. It rewired how crypto startups bootstrapped usage.

narrative.whyChosen: COMP liquidity mining ignited the 2020 DeFi Summer boom.
narrative.whyImportant: Governance tokens became the default growth hack for on-chain protocols.
narrative.problemSolved: DeFi protocols needed decentralized ownership and incentives without venture-only cap tables.
